document.abstract: The media and entertainment industry consumes a significant amount of energy to create, distribute, and present video content to consumers. A large proportion of this energy is used by display devices, notably by the 1.9+ billion displays installed in consumers’ homes globally. The production of light within a display is the main reason for this energy use, independent of display technology. Reducing the global energy use of display devices by any means possible is, therefore, a topic of prime concern. Due to the very large number of displays currently in use, even small reductions per display may end up globally saving enormous amounts of energy. In this spirit, we present a video processing technique that can reduce energy requirements without altering the visual quality of the displayed material. For use cases whereby a viewer would accept a certain loss of visual quality, a user parameter could be exposed that further reduces display energy requirements.

authors.bio: Erik Reinhard is a distinguished scientist at InterDigital Cesson-Sévigné, France, since June 2019. Before that, he held the same position at Technicolor R&I Cesson-Sevigné, starting in July 2013 and before that he held various academic positions at universities and research institutes in Europe and North America. He was the founder and editor-in-chief of ACM Transactions on Applied Perception and authored books on high dynamic range (HDR) imaging, color imaging, computer graphics, and natural image statistics. He has published more than 100 papers and was a member of more than 50 program committees. He was a program co-chair of six conferences and workshops, including the Eurographics Symposium on Rendering 2011. He delivered keynotes at Eurographics 2010, the Computational Color Imaging Workshop 2011, the IS&T European Conference on Color in Graphics, Imaging, and Vision 2012, the IS&T Color Imaging Conference 2022, and the ACM/SIGGRAPH Conference on Visual Media Processing 2022. He is the co-chair of the Rapporteur Group on Energy Aware Broadcasting at ITU-R and co-lead of the Study Mission on Energy Aware Service Delivery and Consumption at DVB. Finally, he won a test of time award for his color transfer paper in IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications
authors.name: Erik Reinhard

authors.bio: Claire-Hélène Demarty is a senior scientist at InterDigital Cesson-Sévigné, France. She graduated from Telecom ParisTech, Paris, France, in 1994 and received a PhD degree in computer science and mathematical morphology, from Mines ParisTech, Paris, in 2000. She joined InterDigital Research & Innovation Center in 2019 as a senior scientist. Before InterDigital, she worked at Technicolor Cesson-Sevigné (2004–2018), LTUTechnologies, Paris (2002–2004), and INRIA Rennes—IRISA, Rennes, France (2003–2004), as a researcher in image analysis and computer vision technologies. Her research focuses on multimedia indexing technologies and perceptual understanding of content, through the use of machine learning, and more recently energy-aware media. She is the author or coauthor of more than 30 papers and holds several patents.
authors.name: Claire-Hélène Demarty

authors.bio: Laurent Blondé is a seasoned principal scientist at InterDigital Cesson-Sévigné, France. He graduated from Institut d’Optique Graduate School Palaiseau, France, in 1985 and received a PhD degree in signal and image processing from Rennes University, Rennes, France. His career has focused in part on various applications of image analysis, synthesis, depth, and color vision, mainly for TV and cinema applications. He has also focused on optics, light propagation understanding, light-matter interaction at wavelength scale, and metasurfaces. In his toolbox, he has image processing, mathematics, teamwork experience, and, mostly, creative thinking. He likes working in an international environment and enjoys interacting with diverse people from various cultures and fields of expertise. He is the author and co-author of papers and patents.
authors.name: Laurent Blondé
